name: Victoria Drew
life: “I still remember missing my cousins' birthday after I left for a better job.” People around the downtown fountain know Victoria by a small Friday habit. Victoria keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I am the cousin with steady wages who went missing first. I owe them a visit without an envelope of excuses.
appearance: Victoria has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a pale blue work shirt with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Victoria presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Victoria carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To visit without replacing conversation with money.
family: Remy Macrae is Victoria’s half-sibling. Victoria asks before bringing somebody along. Remy can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The worker who couldn't read the joke*, Remy says, “I wrote the joke before I knew who would be on shift.”
connections: Noel Gomes. The former babysitter and the salaried cousin can each explain why the first rush of help didn't last.

reactions.situation: The boy's babysitter takes a new job
reactions.response: Victoria helps the family identify the next uncovered school pickup.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Victoria keeps the neighbor's place and finds out whether the stranger needs a different kind of help.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Victoria offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
